findings.finding: The compiled Nevada pathway for this route records that it 'should be routed to legal aid or an attorney because it can involve vacating the conviction, not just sealing it.'
findings.consequence: That is the committed record's own SELF_HELP_STOP answer, so it is the first stop condition, it is on the filing instructions page, and it is quoted rather than paraphrased.

findings.finding: A sex-trafficking fee waiver under NRS 179.245(9) is recorded in this repository, described in the Nevada track registry as a cross-cutting entitlement. This route is NRS 179.247, a different section.
findings.consequence: The waiver is NOT published as this route's fee answer. DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001-A3: holding is per fact, and a line keyed to a different statutory section does not answer this route's question however close the sibling looks. The packet names it as an open question the participant should raise by name, and it is raised for counsel.

findings.finding: The committed contract records that this route has its own nexus and safety conditions and never inherits the deferred-judgment rule.
findings.consequence: No part of the NRS 176.211 deferred-judgment treatment, and no part of the ordinary NRS 179.245 prosecutor-first workflow, was imported into this packet.
